clusters.canonical_name: PE Format and EAT Parsing Foundations
clusters.rationale: Three coverage-gap notes from different SEC670 batches repeatedly surface PE format anatomy (IMAGE_DOS_HEADER, e_lfanew, IMAGE_EXPORT_DIRECTORY, IMAGE_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR) as the prerequisite for loaders, API resolution, and WinDbg introspection.
clusters.consolidated_description:
The vault lacks a reference card documenting the PE binary format as a navigable
concept layer, despite T-004 (PEB Walker), T-007, T-008, and T-013 all depending
on PE anatomy. Required coverage spans IMAGE_DOS_HEADER.e_lfanew at offset 0x3C
→ IMAGE_NT_HEADERS → IMAGE_FILE_HEADER → IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER64 →
IMAGE_DATA_DIRECTORY[16] (EXPORT=0, IMPORT=1, RESOURCE=2, RELOC=5). Specific
traversal targets include IMAGE_EXPORT_DIRECTORY (NumberOfNames /
AddressOfNames / AddressOfNameOrdinals triple-pointer walk for
GetProcAddress-equivalent resolution) and IMAGE_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR's
OriginalFirstThunk / FirstThunk IAT/INT double-chain. The card should also
document WinDbg dx and dt commands against live modules for RVA-to-VA
arithmetic and dumpbin /exports as a static-analysis counterpart.
clusters.technical_anchor: IMAGE_DOS_HEADER.e_lfanew at offset 0x3C → IMAGE_NT_HEADERS → IMAGE_EXPORT_DIRECTORY NumberOfNames/AddressOfNames/AddressOfNameOrdinals triple-pointer walk
clusters.priority_reason: 3+ member notes spanning multiple atlas batches all flag the same foundational prerequisite gap; concept card that unblocks four existing T-NNN cards.

clusters.canonical_name: Evasion Stack Sequence Convergence
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence: SEC670's evasion roadmap (UnhookTheHook → No Caller ID → AMSI No More) mirrors T-016's evasion suite ordering exactly, validating the vault's structural choices.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Section 5's pedagogic evasion sequence — NTDLL unhook → caller/stack
spoofing → AMSI bypass — converges precisely with T-016's EDR evasion suite
implementation order. The convergence validates both the technical sequencing
(EDR hook removal must precede stack-spoofing because spoofed calls re-enter
hooked NTDLL paths) and the pedagogic scaffolding. The card should document why
this order is mandatory: AMSI bypasses executed before unhooking NTDLL's
AmsiScanBuffer trampoline re-enter attacker code via the still-hooked
indirection, leaking the patch itself to the EDR's hook-side telemetry.
clusters.technical_anchor: NTDLL unhook → stack/arg spoofing → AMSI bypass execution-order dependency (AmsiScanBuffer trampoline re-entry hazard)
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but high-signal cross-source convergence validating existing card structure.

clusters.canonical_name: Windows API Fundamentals as Prerequisite Layer
clusters.rationale: Two coverage-gap notes flag missing prerequisite material on calling conventions, WinDef.h macros, Windows data type aliases, and SAL annotations across SEC670 batches.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 devotes an entire module to Win32 programming prerequisites that the
vault assumes but does not document: x64 calling convention (RCX/RDX/R8/R9 +
shadow space 0x20 bytes), WinDef.h macros (DECLARE_HANDLE, MAKEINTRESOURCE,
HIWORD/LOWORD), Windows data type aliases (DWORD=uint32_t, LPVOID=void*,
HANDLE=PVOID), and the Win32 → NTAPI translation layer (OpenProcess →
NtOpenProcess, CreateFile → NtCreateFile). This material directly gates
T-001/T-002 (syscalls), T-003 (API hashing), T-004 (PEB walk), T-013 (PE
loader), and T-016 (evasion suite). A standalone reference card with the
typedef chain and the user32→ntdll call-down diagram would make those cards
navigable without prior Windows programming background.
clusters.technical_anchor: x64 calling convention RCX/RDX/R8/R9 + 0x20 shadow space; Win32→NTAPI translation (OpenProcess→NtOpenProcess, CreateFile→NtCreateFile)
clusters.priority_reason: 2 member notes spanning multiple batches; unblocks multiple operational cards.

clusters.canonical_name: Win32 Error Handling Model (HRESULT/LSTATUS/BOOL + GetLastError)
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: the HRESULT/LSTATUS/BOOL tristate error model recurs across SEC670 units but is not documented as a reference concept in the vault.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 devotes substantial material to the Win32 error model: BOOL returns +
GetLastError (DWORD thread-local via TEB->LastErrorValue at offset 0x34),
HRESULT (SUCCEEDED/FAILED macros against the SEVERITY bit at 0x80000000),
LSTATUS for registry APIs (ERROR_SUCCESS=0), and FormatMessageW with
FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM for symbolic lookup. Implant code should call
GetLastError immediately after a failed Win32 call because the per-thread
value is overwritten by subsequent calls. The card should document the TEB
LastErrorValue field, the HRESULT facility/code split (Facility at bits
16-30, Code at bits 0-15), and the FORMAT_MESSAGE_ALLOCATE_BUFFER pattern.
clusters.technical_anchor: TEB->LastErrorValue at offset 0x34 (per-thread GetLastError storage); HRESULT SEVERITY bit at 0x80000000; FormatMessageW FORMAT_MESSAGE_FROM_SYSTEM
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton foundational concept; not directly mapped to existing T-NNN.

clusters.canonical_name: Rust as Offensive and Defensive Language Trend
clusters.rationale: Singleton emerging note on Rust adoption in Windows kernel and offensive tooling; HUGIN vault itself is implemented in Rust.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Unit 33 flags Rust as a transformative language for both offensive and
defensive tooling, citing Windows kernel components being rewritten in Rust
(win32kbase GDI region, kernel sample components). The HUGIN vault itself is
implemented in Rust, and several modern red-team tools follow the same pattern.
The card should document the specific Rust features that matter offensively:
zero-cost abstractions for position-independent shellcode generators, cargo's
deterministic build graph (single reproducible binary), the unsafe{} escape
hatch for raw pointer derefs equivalent to C void*, and the borrow checker's
elimination of use-after-free bugs that plague C implants. Detection
implications: Rust binaries have distinctive panic_str and core::panicking
symbols that EDR vendors are beginning to signature.
clusters.technical_anchor: Rust unsafe{} block for raw pointer derefs; cargo deterministic build graph; panic_str/core::panicking symbol artifacts in release binaries
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton trend observation; not directly mappable to existing T-NNN.

clusters.canonical_name: Binary Patching as Cross-Cutting Evasion Primitive
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 introduces binary patching as a foundational module distinct from hooking; T-016 lists adjacent primitives but not patching itself.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Unit 24 treats binary patching as its own evasion primitive distinct
from API hooking: in-place modification of instruction bytes at the function
prologue (jmp/call trampoline) or within a code cave (overwritten with NOPs +
ret 0x12 for AMSI). T-016 currently lists AMSI, ETW, stack spoofing, PEB unlink,
NTDLL unhook, and handle blocking but omits the underlying byte-patching
primitive. The card should distinguish patching (write to .text at VA) from
hooking (write a jmp indirection through Detours-style trampoline) — patching
is one-shot and persistent across process lifetime, while hooking requires
runtime indirection per call. Specific examples: AmsiScanBuffer prologue
patched with mov eax, AMSI_RESULT_CLEAN; ret; EtwEventWrite patched with ret
0x00 (NtTraceEvent returns STATUS_SUCCESS on 0).
clusters.technical_anchor: In-place prologue patch of AmsiScanBuffer with mov eax, AMSI_RESULT_CLEAN; ret (or xor eax,eax; ret); EtwEventWrite patched to ret returning STATUS_SUCCESS
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but fills gap in flagship T-016 evasion suite.

clusters.canonical_name: Shellcode Authoring in C with Compiler/Linker Flag Mastery
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence on SEC670's shellcode-in-C module emphasizing flag overrides to suppress CRT emissions; aligns with Rust PIC shellcode approach.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Units 28-30 frame shellcode creation in C as a discipline of compiler
and linker flag overrides to suppress CRT initialization, exception tables,
and relocation fixups that would emit position-dependent code. Required flag
matrix: /MT (static CRT, but strip later with /NODEFAULTLIB), /GS- (disable
stack cookies/__security_init_cookie), /Zi (debug info, PDB stripped
post-link), /ENTRY:main (override CRT default entry), /ALIGN:16 (shellcode
section alignment), /EMITPOGPHASEINFO- (no profile-guided data),
/SUBSYSTEM:NATIVE (skip Win32 loader). Post-link processing via sgn.exe or
donut pattern_loader shellcode transformer. The card should document the
resulting x64 position-independent shellcode layout: base address obtained
via call/pop pattern, no .rdata relocations (string literals emitted inline
in .text), no IAT (all APIs resolved via PEB walk).
clusters.technical_anchor: /MT /GS- /Zi /ENTRY:main /ALIGN:16 /SUBSYSTEM:NATIVE linker flag matrix; post-link sgn.exe shellcode transformation; call/pop pattern for base-address recovery
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but converges with T-021 shellcode generator implementation.

clusters.canonical_name: Native Subsystem (IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM_NATIVE) Implant Entry Points
clusters.rationale: Singleton emerging-tradecraft note: native subsystem executables bypass Win32 loader, receiving PEB directly at entry; not documented in T-001..T-074.
clusters.consolidated_description:
Native-subsystem executables (IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM_NATIVE in
IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER.Subsystem) receive the PEB pointer directly as
NtProcessStartup's first parameter — no CRT, no Win32 loader, no
kernel32!CreateProcess call path. Entry signature is
NTSTATUS NtProcessStartup(PPEB peb). This pattern lets implants skip the
standard Win32 module-load telemetry (Sysmon EID 1 with ImageLoad events
for kernel32/user32/gdi32), presenting as a standalone native image.
Trade-offs: must hand-resolve all imports via PEB->Ldr->InLoadOrderModuleList
walk (smss.exe / csrss.exe / wininit.exe are the only legitimate native
binaries, so process name selection matters). The card should document the
SUBSYSTEM field location at IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER offset 0x44 (PE32) / 0x5C
(PE32+) and the /SUBSYSTEM:NATIVE linker flag equivalent.
clusters.technical_anchor: IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM_NATIVE (0x03) at IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER.Subsystem; entry point NTSTATUS NtProcessStartup(PPEB peb) bypasses Win32 loader
clusters.priority_reason: Novel capability not in T-001..T-074; bypasses Win32 loader telemetry; rare legitimate usage makes it high-signal.

clusters.canonical_name: Reflective DLL Injection as Elevated T-013 Family Member
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 documents RDI mechanics in depth but T-013 only lists 'PE Loader' as one of 14 references; no dedicated RDI card.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Units 19 and 20 cover RDI mechanics in detail: a
position-independent ReflectiveLoader() function bootstraps itself by
walking PEB->Ldr to find ntdll/kernel32, manually parsing the embedded PE
headers (IMAGE_DOS_HEADER, IMAGE_NT_HEADERS, IMAGE_SECTION_HEADER array),
VirtualAlloc'ing RWX target memory, copying headers + sections, processing
IMAGE_BASE_RELOCATION blocks (applying delta to IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64
entries), walking IMAGE_IMPORT_DESCRIPTOR chain with
LoadLibraryA/GetProcAddress, calling DllMain(DLL_PROCESS_ATTACH). The card
should document the bootstrapping problem: the loader itself runs before
its own imports are resolved, so the first PEB walk uses only intrinsic
pointer arithmetic — no libc, no Win32 calls until after LoadLibraryA is
resolved. T-013 mentions RDI as one of 14 references but a dedicated card
with the bootstrap order would close the gap.
clusters.technical_anchor: Position-independent ReflectiveLoader() with PEB->Ldr walk to resolve ntdll/kernel32; IMAGE_BASE_RELOCATION block processing with IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64 delta fixups
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but fills dedicated card slot in T-013 PE loader family.

clusters.canonical_name: UAC Bypass Research via UACMe Project Corpus
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence: SEC670 references UACMe's FusionScanDirectory primitive; vault mentions CMSTP bypass in T-023 but lacks the UACMe corpus as a research reference.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Unit 4 references the UACMe project's FusionScanDirectory function as
a UAC-bypass research primitive for enumerating auto-elevated binaries. The
vault's T-021 mentions UAC bypass and T-023 covers UAC bypass via CMSTP,
but neither documents the broader UACMe methodology catalog (70+ numbered
techniques indexed by method: IFileOperation COM elevation, ICMLuaUtil
ShellExecute, IDispatch auto-elevation, sdclt.exe registry hijack,
fodhelper.exe DLL load). The card should document the auto-elevated binary
discovery workflow: enumerate IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER for
Subsystem=IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM_WINDOWS_GUI + the
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Fusion\AutoElevate=1 binaries,
identify each binary's missing DLL/progID/registry gaps, and craft a bypass
per gap. Specific UACMe techniques worth indexing as sub-techniques: method
55 (fodhelper.exe + HKCU\Environment\windir), method 56 (sdclt.exe +
HKCU\...\Shell\open\command).
clusters.technical_anchor: UACMe FusionScanDirectory enumerating AutoElevate=1 binaries; fodhelper.exe + HKCU\Environment\windir overwrite (UACMe method 55)
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but references public tooling (UACMe) with 70+ enumerated techniques.

clusters.canonical_name: CNG/BCrypt as Modern Shellcode Crypto API
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 documents full BCrypt AES sequence; vault's T-021 uses Rust crypto crate instead, leaving shellcode-scoped crypto undocumented.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670's AES walkthrough uses the full BCrypt API sequence:
BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider(BCRYPT_AES_ALGORITHM) →
BCryptSetProperty(BCRYPT_CHAINING_MODE=BCRYPT_CHAIN_MODE_GCM) →
BCryptGenerateSymmetricKey(hKey) → BCryptDecrypt(hKey, pbIV, pbAuthData,
pbCipherText). The vault's T-021 documents AES-256-GCM via a Rust crypto
crate (presumably aes-gcm), which is unavailable to position-independent
shellcode or pre-IAT-resolution code. The card should document the BCrypt
API call sequence, the BCRYPT_AUTHENTICATED_CIPHER_MODE_INFO struct
initialization (pbNonce, pbAuthData, pbTag, cbTag=16), and the alternative
pathway via CNG: NCryptOpenStorageProvider + NCryptOpenKey for
DPAPI-equivalent key isolation. Shellcode-specific guidance: bcrypt.dll is
loaded early by wininit.exe so PEB-walk resolution is reliable.
clusters.technical_anchor: BCryptOpenAlgorithmProvider(BCRYPT_AES_ALGORITHM) → BCryptSetProperty(BCRYPT_CHAIN_MODE_GCM) → BCRYPT_AUTHENTICATED_CIPHER_MODE_INFO struct with pbNonce/pbTag (cbTag=16)
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but covers shellcode-scoped crypto alternative to Rust crypto crate.

clusters.canonical_name: SAL Annotation Literacy as API-Contract Reading Skill
clusters.rationale: Two coverage-gap notes from different atlas batches surface SAL annotations as the missing reading skill for hand-binding NT APIs.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 dedicates a section to Microsoft's Source Annotation Language as the
canonical method for reading Windows SDK header signatures when hand-binding
NT APIs (vs FFI declarations or dumpbin /exports). The annotation set
includes _In_, _Out_, _Inout_, _In_opt_, _In_reads_(N), _Out_writes_(N),
_In_bytecount_(cb), _deref_out_. The card should document each annotation's
caller obligation: _In_ = caller provides initialized buffer; _Out_ = callee
writes, caller allocates; _Inout_ = callee may read+write; _In_reads_(N) =
caller-provided buffer of N elements; _In_opt_ = NULL permitted. Specific
examples from T-004/T-013/T-016 hand-bound APIs:
NtQueryInformationProcess(ProcessBasicInformation) expects _In_ HANDLE
ProcessHandle, _In_ PROCESSINFOCLASS ProcessInformationClass,
_Out_writes_bytes_(ProcessInformationLength) PVOID ProcessInformation,
_In_ ULONG ProcessInformationLength, _Out_opt_ PULONG ReturnLength.
Misreading these contracts causes silent truncation or buffer overflow.
clusters.technical_anchor: _In_/_Out_/_Inout_/_In_reads_(N)/_Out_writes_(N) annotations on NtQueryInformationProcess signature (_In_ HANDLE, _In_ PROCESSINFOCLASS, _Out_writes_bytes_ PVOID, _In_ ULONG, _Out_opt_ PULONG)
clusters.priority_reason: 2 member notes from different atlas batches; unblocks multiple syscall/API hand-binding cards.

clusters.canonical_name: AMSI Bypass via Code Caves and Function Hooking
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence: SEC670 lists 'AMSI No More' using code caves/function hooking, distinct from hardware breakpoint and PAGE_GUARD bypass pathways in vault.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670's 'AMSI No More' bootcamp exercise uses code caves and function
hooking to disable AMSI in a PowerShell process — distinct from the vault's
amsi_hbp.rs (hardware breakpoint) and PAGE_GUARD-based pathways. The
code-cave variant overwrites bytes within AmsiScanBuffer's prologue
(typically the 5-byte mov instruction fetching AmsiContextHeader) with a
jmp rel32 to a cave in unused .text padding that returns
AMSI_RESULT_CLEAN (forcing 0x80070057 → S_OK). Function-hooking variant
installs a trampoline at AmsiScanBuffer via detours-style jmp [ptr],
redirecting to a stub that returns S_OK + zeroed scan buffer. The card
should document detection surfaces: hardware breakpoints leave
PROCESS_HARDWARE_INFORMATION_DR7/DR8 set in TEB, while code caves leave
.text section RWX permissions and byte-diff hash mismatches against clean
amsi.dll.
clusters.technical_anchor: Code-cave patch of AmsiScanBuffer prologue (5-byte mov instruction) → jmp rel32 to cave returning AMSI_RESULT_CLEAN (E_INVALIDARG)
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but documents a distinct AMSI bypass mechanism not covered by existing amsi_hbp.rs.

clusters.canonical_name: Advanced Capability as Last-Resort Tradecraft
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence: SEC670 frames manual image loading + API hook re-implementation + C2 callbacks + shellcode execution as last-resort capabilities for hardened targets.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Unit 31 frames a tier of capabilities as last-resort tradecraft
reserved for hardened targets where standard injection fails: manual image
loading (T-013 PE loader family), API hook re-implementation (inline detours
on NTDLL exports), C2 callback dispatch from within hooked API returns, and
shellcode execution via APC queueing (T-007). The convergence with the
vault's broader 'last-resort' framing (T-007/T-013/T-016/T-022) suggests
the card should document the decision tree: when does an operator escalate
from CreateRemoteThread+LoadLibrary (loud, EDR-detected) to RDI (medium,
PE-sieve detected) to threadless export overwrite (quiet, requires shared
module presence). The escalation matrix maps detection surfaces to
technique selection.
clusters.technical_anchor: Escalation matrix: CreateRemoteThread+LoadLibrary → RDI → threadless export overwrite; detection surface to technique selection mapping
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton decision-tree card; lower operational specificity than implementation cards.

clusters.canonical_name: Handle Leak Discipline After CreateProcess
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: PROCESS_INFORMATION returns hProcess and hThread kernel handles that leak in caller's handle table; not documented in injection cards.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Units 39-40 emphasize that CreateProcess returns a
PROCESS_INFORMATION struct with two kernel handles — hProcess and hThread
— that must be closed via CloseHandle when no longer required, or they
leak in the caller's handle table indefinitely. Handle leaks are an
operational opsec hazard: EDR vendors querying
NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemHandleInformation) on a long-lived process
will see accumulating handles to spawned children, revealing injection
ancestry. The vault's T-013/T-014/T-015 injection cards create processes
via CREATE_SUSPENDED for hollowing/thread-hijacking patterns but do not
document the cleanup discipline. Specific guidance: after NtResumeProcess,
wait for child exit (WaitForSingleObject(hThread, INFINITE)) THEN
CloseHandle(hThread); CloseHandle(hProcess);. Failure to wait before
close leaves zombie threads.
clusters.technical_anchor: CloseHandle on PROCESS_INFORMATION.hProcess and PROCESS_INFORMATION.hThread after NtResumeProcess + WaitForSingleObject(INFINITE)
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but applies to 3 flagship injection cards; opsec hazard if ignored.

clusters.canonical_name: CREATE_SUSPENDED as Cross-Source Foundational Primitive
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence: CREATE_SUSPENDED appears as primary CreateProcess flag, foundational to T-012 (Early Cascade) and T-013 (hollow process) injection.
clusters.consolidated_description:
CREATE_SUSPENDED (0x00000004) appears as the primary creation flag on
CreateProcess across SEC670 material, foundational to T-012 (Early Cascade
Injection) and T-013 (process hollowing). The flag causes the kernel to
initialize the new process and its main thread but suspend at the
LdrpInitialize process-launch APC dispatch — before any user-mode code in
the new process executes. The vault uses this primitive implicitly in
hollow.rs but does not document the suspension point. The card should
document the suspension mechanics: NtCreateProcessEx returns
STATUS_SUCCESS with the thread in a Waiting state (THREAD_STATE=5);
NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation) shows the new process
with no loaded modules beyond ntdll.dll; LdrpInitialize's APC is queued but
not dispatched until NtResumeProcess triggers KiUserApcDispatcher.
Operator consequence: between CREATE_SUSPENDED and NtResumeProcess, the
process is in a deterministic uninitialized state ideal for image-base
replacement, PEB unlinking, and module-list hollowing.
clusters.technical_anchor: CREATE_SUSPENDED=0x00000004 suspends new process at LdrpInitialize APC dispatch; thread in Waiting state (THREAD_STATE=5); NtResumeProcess triggers KiUserApcDispatcher
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but cross-source convergence on a primitive underlying 2 flagship injection cards.

clusters.canonical_name: COM CoInitialize/CoCreateInstance Baseline Knowledge
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 documents the canonical COM instantiation flow that T-017 (COM hijack) and T-008 (threadless export) depend on but assume.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670's WUA UpdateSession material documents the canonical COM instantiation
flow: CoInitializeEx(NULL, COINIT_APARTMENTTHREADED) →
CoCreateInstance(CLSID_UpdateSession, pUnkOuter=NULL, CLSCTX_LOCAL_SERVER,
IID_IUpdateSession, &pSession) → pSession->CreateUpdateSearcher() via
vtable[N] dispatch. The vault's T-017 COM hijack persistence and T-008
threadless export overwrite both assume this flow without documenting it.
The card should cover the vtable layout (QueryInterface at offset 0, AddRef
at 8, Release at 16, then custom methods from 24), the CLSCTX flag
semantics (CLSCTX_INPROC_SERVER=0x1 vs CLSCTX_LOCAL_SERVER=0x4 → surrogate
process selection), and the registry backing store at
HKCR\CLSID\{CLSID}\InprocServer32 (default value = absolute DLL path,
ThreadingModel = Apartment/Free/Both). Hijack primitive: write a DLL path
to InprocServer32\Default that supersedes the legitimate one in HKLM with
HKCU precedence.
clusters.technical_anchor: CoCreateInstance(CLSID, NULL, CLSCTX, IID, &pInterface) vtable dispatch (QueryInterface/AddRef/Release at offsets 0/8/16); HKCR\CLSID\{CLSID}\InprocServer32\ThreadingModel
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but unblocks 2 existing cards (T-008, T-017).

clusters.canonical_name: PE-sieve as Defensive Validation Scanner
clusters.rationale: Two coverage-gap notes flag PE-sieve as the missing defensive validation tool; T-007/T-013/T-016 document offensive techniques without the corresponding detection tooling.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Lab 1.1 dedicates a unit to PE-sieve (hasherezade's open-source memory
scanner) as the canonical defensive validation tool for injection detection.
PE-sieve walks the loaded module list via
NtQueryInformationProcess(ProcessMappedInformation), then for each module
compares the in-memory image against the on-disk PE file (byte-diff hash
over .text section, IAT mismatch detection, hollowed process detection via
PEB->Ldr entry mismatch against actual loaded base). Detection surfaces:
classic DLL injection (extra module in PEB but not on disk), process
hollowing (PEB->Ldr entry matches on-disk file but in-memory image differs),
reflective DLL injection (no PEB entry but executable memory region with PE
headers). Operators should run PE-sieve /imp /hooks /threads against their
own implants during testing to verify evasion claims. The card should
document the specific PE-sieve command-line matrix and the resulting report
sections.
clusters.technical_anchor: PE-sieve: NtQueryInformationProcess(ProcessMappedInformation) + on-disk PE byte-diff hash over .text section + PEB->Ldr vs actual loaded base mismatch
clusters.priority_reason: 2 member notes from different batches; closes validation-tooling gap for 4 injection/evasion cards.

clusters.canonical_name: SEC670 Convergence on Injection and Evasion Tradecraft
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence: SEC670 labs (Call_DirectInjection, APCInjection, ThreadHijacker, ClassicDLLInjection, UnhookTheHook, AMSI No More) cover same technique space as T-007/T-013/T-016.
clusters.consolidated_description:
Multiple SEC670 labs converge on the same injection and evasion technique
space as the vault's T-007/T-013/T-016: Call_DirectInjection (direct syscall
injection, mirrors T-001/T-007), APCInjection (APC queue injection, mirrors
T-007 APC variant), ThreadHijacker (thread context RIP overwrite, mirrors
T-014), ClassicDLLInjection (LoadLibrary via CreateRemoteThread, mirrors
T-007 baseline), The Loader (manual PE loader, mirrors T-013 RDI),
UnhookTheHook (NTDLL .text section overwrite from clean on-disk copy,
mirrors T-016), AMSI No More (AmsiScanBuffer patching, mirrors T-016). The
convergence validates the vault's technique categorization but suggests the
vault could document lab-to-technique mapping as a pedagogic bridge. The
card should be a cross-reference table linking each SEC670 lab exercise to
its corresponding T-NNN card.
clusters.technical_anchor: Lab-to-technique mapping: Call_DirectInjection↔T-001/T-007, APCInjection↔T-007 APC variant, ThreadHijacker↔T-014, UnhookTheHook↔T-016 (NTDLL .text overwrite from on-disk clean copy)
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton cross-reference card; lower operational specificity than implementation cards.

clusters.canonical_name: Windows Service (SCM) Persistence as Distinct Layer
clusters.rationale: Four coverage-gap notes from different batches flag service persistence as missing from T-017's five-layer suite; SEC670 dedicates multiple units to SCM programming.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 dedicates multiple units to the Windows Service Control Manager
programming model: ServiceMain entry point,
StartServiceControlDispatcher (binding SERVICE_TABLE_ENTRY array),
RegisterServiceCtrlHandlerEx (registering HandlerFunction callback),
SetServiceStatus (SERVICE_RUNNING/SERVICE_STOPPED state machine), and the
SCM-RPC protocol. Service persistence variants include: (1) classic —
register a binary at
HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\{svc}\ImagePath, Start=2
(SERVICE_AUTO_START), Type=0x10 (SERVICE_WIN32_OWN_PROCESS); (2) shared
process — Type=0x20 (SERVICE_WIN32_SHARE_PROCESS) for blending with
svchost; (3) service-binary patching — modify an existing service's
ImagePath to point at attacker-controlled binary preserving the original
service name for cover. The vault's T-017 covers COM hijack, NTFS EA,
schtask, TLS callback, and PhantomPersist but omits services. Card should
document detection: Sysmon EID 1 + EID 3 + ImagePath mismatch against
signed service binary inventory.
clusters.technical_anchor: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\{svc}\ImagePath (Start=2 SERVICE_AUTO_START, Type=0x10 SERVICE_WIN32_OWN_PROCESS); ServiceMain/StartServiceControlDispatcher/RegisterServiceCtrlHandlerEx API sequence
clusters.priority_reason: 4 member notes from different batches; flagship persistence card T-017 has explicit gap for this category.

clusters.canonical_name: AppInit_DLLs Persistence
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 lists AppInit_DLLs across multiple units (InitToWinit bootcamp challenge, Units 6/16/33); T-017 covers COM hijack/NTFS EA/schtask/TLS/Phantom but not AppInit_DLLs.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Units 1, 6, 16, and 33 list AppInit_DLLs as a persistence and
DLL-execution foothold, with the InitToWinit bootcamp challenge centering on
the technique. The vault's T-017 Five-Layer Persistence card covers COM
hijack, NTFS EA, schtask, TLS callback, and PhantomPersist but omits
AppInit_DLLs. The card should document:
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows\AppInit_DLLs
(REG_SZ space-separated DLL paths) + AppInit_DLLs\RequireSignedDlls
(REG_DWORD 0/1) + LoadAppInit_DLLs (REG_DWORD 0/1). Mechanism:
user32.dll!_LoadAppInitDlls on process map, walks AppInit_DLLs in any
process that links user32.dll (i.e., most GUI processes). Modern
constraint: Win10 1709+ restricts AppInit_DLLs to LoadAppInit_DLLs=1 in the
same HKLM key, and only loads in processes with matching bitness.
Detection: Sysmon EID 7 (ImageLoaded) for AppInit_DLLs-listed binaries +
registry monitor on the AppInit_DLLs value.
clusters.technical_anchor: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows\AppInit_DLLs (REG_SZ space-separated paths) + LoadAppInit_DLLs/RequireSignedDlls REG_DWORD; user32.dll!_LoadAppInitDlls loads at user32 map

clusters.canonical_name: Windows Object Manager as Foundational Reference Card

clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Book 1 devotes multiple units to the Windows Object Manager — the
executive subsystem standardizing object headers, bodies, handle tables,
and ACL-gated access for 4000+ object types (Process, Thread, File, Token,
Event, Mutant, Section, Key, etc.). The vault's T-016 (handle blocking),

via handle ops), T-013 (PE loader using Section objects), and T-004 (PEB

card should document: executive objects vs kernel objects (USER-objects vs
GDI-objects are non-executive), the OBJECT_HEADER structure (with Type
index, NameInfoOffset, SecurityDescriptorOffset, QuotaInfoOffset fields
preceding the body), the per-process handle table (PspCidTable via
EPROCESS->HandleTable → PHANDLE_TABLE), and the ObpCreateHandle flow
(ExCreateHandle → OBJECT_HEADER->SecurityDescriptor check →
ObpIncrementHandleCount). Reference: NtQueryObject/ObjectAllInformation
returns the entire OM view.

clusters.canonical_name: DLL Search Order as Standalone Tradecraft
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 documents 5-step DLL search order underpinning proxy DLL loading (T-016) and DLL hijacking broadly; vault lacks the search-order mechanism card.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Unit 34 documents the 5-step DLL search order that underpins proxy
DLL loading (T-016 proxy_dll.rs) and DLL hijacking broadly: (1) directory
of the calling process (EXE directory); (2) SystemDirectory
(C:\Windows\System32); (3) Windows directory (C:\Windows); (4) current
working directory; (5) PATH. Modifiers: SafeDllSearchMode
(HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session
Manager\SafeDllSearchMode=1 by default since XP SP2 — moves CWD to
position 5, after PATH) and KnownDlls
(HKLM\SYSTEM\...\KnownDlls list of forcibly shared DLLs, bypasses search
entirely by mapping from KnownDlls\*.dl_ section objects). The vault's
proxy_dll.rs implements the technique but lacks the search-order mechanism
documentation. The card should also cover
SetDefaultDllDirectories(LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_USER_DIRS) for runtime
override, AddDllDirectory, and the LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_* flag matrix on
LoadLibraryEx.
clusters.technical_anchor: 5-step DLL search order; SafeDllSearchMode registry value (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager); KnownDlls section object mapping bypass
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but underpins flagship T-016 proxy_dll.rs implementation.

clusters.canonical_name: Process Enumeration Method Comparison (Toolhelp vs WTS vs NT)
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence: SEC670 compares CreateToolhelp32Snapshot vs WTSEnumerateProcesses vs NtQuerySystemInformation enumeration methods.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 compares three process-enumeration APIs with different detection
surfaces and outputs. CreateToolhelp32Snapshot (kernel32) — wraps
NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation), returns
PROCESSENTRY32W (szExeFile, th32ProcessID, th32ParentProcessID,
cntThreads, pcPriClassBase); calls NtClose on the snapshot handle
(must-close or handle leak). WTSEnumerateProcesses(WTS_CURRENT_SERVER) —
server-side RPC via TermSrv, returns WTS_PROCESS_INFO array with SID,
SessionId; useful for terminal-services hosts where
CreateToolhelp32Snapshot is filtered. NtQuerySystemInformation
(SystemProcessInformation) — direct syscall, returns
SYSTEM_PROCESS_INFORMATION array with NextEntryOffset relative
traversal, NumberOfThreads, HandleCount, ImageName (UNICODE_STRING may
be empty for System/Idle processes). The card should document the
trade-off matrix: toolhelp = most common but observable via
NtQuerySystemInformation hook; WTS = quietest but requires RpcRt4.dll
bind; native syscall = fastest but no parent/SID resolution.
clusters.technical_anchor: CreateToolhelp32Snapshot (kernel32 wraps NtQuerySystemInformation); WTSEnumerateProcesses (TermSrv RPC); NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation) with SYSTEM_PROCESS_INFORMATION NextEntryOffset relative traversal
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but compares 3 enumeration methods with distinct detection surfaces.

clusters.canonical_name: Registry Watchdog Detection via RegNotifyChangeKeyValue
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 documents RegNotifyChangeKeyValue as defensive primitive for registry change notification; vault's T-017 persistence lacks detection counterpart.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 documents RegNotifyChangeKeyValue as a defensive primitive for
receiving notifications on registry key changes. Signature:
RegNotifyChangeKeyValue(hKey, bWatchSubtree=TRUE,
dwNotifyFilter=REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_NAME|REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_ATTRIBUTES|
REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_LAST_SET|REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_SECURITY, hEvent=NULL,
fAsynchronous=FALSE). When synchronous, the call blocks the calling
thread until a matching change occurs. For asynchronous mode, pass an
event handle (CreateEvent + SetEvent on change) and fAsynchronous=TRUE.
Detection surface: the watchdog sees the persistence mechanism's registry
write, including value name, before/after content, and timestamp. The
vault's T-017 covers persistence mechanisms (COM hijack, NTFS EA,
schtask, TLS callback, PhantomPersist) but lacks the corresponding
detection primitive. Operators can use the same API on the operator side
to monitor for defender blue-team registry queries against persistence
keys. Card should document the per-key filter mask matrix and the
per-key root handles (HKLM\SOFTWARE\...\Run vs HKCU\...\RunOnce).
clusters.technical_anchor: RegNotifyChangeKeyValue(hKey, bWatchSubtree=TRUE, dwNotifyFilter=REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_LAST_SET|REG_NOTIFY_CHANGE_NAME, hEvent, fAsynchronous)
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but provides detection counterpart to flagship T-017 persistence card.

clusters.canonical_name: Windows Dispatcher Quantum and Priority Model
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 documents Windows dispatcher preemptive priority-based scheduling and quantum allocation; foundational to T-007/T-012/T-013 thread timing.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 devotes multiple units to the Windows dispatcher's preemptive
priority-based scheduling, quantum allocation in clock cycles, and
preemption events. The vault's thread-pool and APC techniques (T-007,
T-012, T-013) all depend on dispatcher behavior for timing but do not
document it. The card should cover: 32 priority levels (0-31, with 16-31
realtime, 1-15 variable, 0 reserved for System), quantum target = clock
ticks (default ~12 ticks on workstation, ~36 on server, ~6 on background,
controlled via
HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\PriorityControl\Win32PrioritySeparation),
the KPRCB DispatcherReadyQueueHead[32] array, and the KiDispatcherLock
acquisition before a context switch. Operator implication: APC injection is
dispatched during the target thread's next quantum at PASSIVE_LEVEL when in
a wait state; boosting thread priority via
NtSetInformationProcess(ProcessBasePriority) lets an APC fire faster but
increases dispatcher observability.
clusters.technical_anchor: KPRCB DispatcherReadyQueueHead[32] array; quantum target via Win32PrioritySeparation (default 12 ticks workstation); KiDispatcherLock acquisition before context switch
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton foundational concept card; lower operational specificity.

clusters.canonical_name: Heaven's Gate (Wow64 32-to-64-bit Syscall Transition)
clusters.rationale: Singleton emerging-tradecraft note: SEC670 documents Heaven's Gate as Wow64-mediated 0x33 segment transition for 32-to-64 syscall dispatch; distinct from T-002 Hell's/Halo's/Tartarus Gate SSN resolution.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Unit 34 documents Heaven's Gate as the Wow64-mediated transition from
32-bit code to 64-bit syscall dispatch via the 0x33 segment selector in the
32-bit TEB. The 32-bit TEB has two code-segment selectors (Teb32 and Teb64
selectors in TEB fields at offsets 0xC0/0xE0); jumping to a far32 ptr with
selector 0x33 switches CS to the 64-bit segment, allowing execution of
native 64-bit syscall instructions (mov eax, SS; syscall) bypassing the
32-bit Wow64 thunk layer (ntdll!Nt* stub → wow64!Nt* thunk →
wow64cpu!TurboDispatch → 64-bit ntdll). The vault's T-002
(Hell's/Halo's/Tartarus Gate) addresses SSN resolution via unhooked Nt*
stub hashing, which is a different problem (resolving syscall numbers
without Nt* stubs in memory) vs Heaven's Gate (bypassing Wow64 layer for
direct 64-bit syscall dispatch from 32-bit shellcode). The card should
document the 0x33 selector jump pattern, the 0x23 reverse transition, and
modern Win10+ mitigations.
clusters.technical_anchor: 0x33 segment selector in 32-bit TEB; far jump with CS=0x33 switches to 64-bit segment for direct syscall dispatch bypassing Wow64 thunk layer
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but distinct from T-002 (resolves Wow64 layer bypass vs SSN resolution); named technique with public tooling.

(SACL_AUDIT_ACE with ACCESS_MASK for success/failure audits), the

clusters.canonical_name: SEC670 Thread Creation Internals as Cross-Reference
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence: SEC670 Books 1+3 document NtCreateThreadEx → PspCreateThread creation flow with suspended/resumed APC dispatch; cross-reference for T-007/T-012/T-013/T-014.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 Books 1 and 3 document the NtCreateThreadEx → PspCreateThread
creation flow with suspended-then-resumed semantics and the APC-queue
dispatch mechanism during thread quantum. The flow:
NtCreateThreadEx(ThreadHandle, DesiredAccess, ObjectAttributes,
ProcessHandle, StartAddress, Argument, CreateFlags, ZeroBits,
StackSize, MaxStackSize, AttributeList) → NtCreateThreadEx calls
PspCreateThread → PspCreateThread allocates ETHREAD, initializes Tcb
(KTHREAD), sets StartAddress, queues a user-mode APC
(PspUserThreadStartup) that runs LdrpInitialize for module load before
StartAddress. If CreateFlags has CREATE_SUSPENDED (bit 0), thread enters
Waiting state and APC is not dispatched until NtResumeThread →
KiUserApcDispatcher pulls the queued APC. This flow is foundational to
T-007 (APC injection), T-012 (Early Cascade — queue user APC before
thread runs), T-013 (hollowing on suspended initial thread), T-014 (RIP
overwrite on suspended thread via SetThreadContext). The card should
document the APC queue location
(KTHREAD->ApcState.ApcListHead[UserMode]) and the CreateFlags bit
layout.
clusters.technical_anchor: NtCreateThreadEx → PspCreateThread → PspUserThreadStartup APC queued at KTHREAD->ApcState.ApcListHead[UserMode]; CREATE_SUSPENDED bit 0 of CreateFlags holds APC dispatch
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton cross-reference for 4 injection cards; documents the suspended-APC mechanism.

clusters.canonical_name: WMI Event Subscription Persistence
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 dedicates Section 4 module to WMI Event Subscriptions with canonical filter/consumer/binding triad; T-017 lacks WMI persistence.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 dedicates a Section 4 module to WMI Event Subscriptions as a
persistence vector with the canonical filter/consumer/binding triad. The
vault's T-017 (Five-Layer Persistence) covers COM hijack, NTFS EA,
schtask, TLS callback, and PhantomPersist but not WMI event
subscription. The card should document: __EventFilter instance in
root\subscription namespace (QueryLanguage=WQL, Query="SELECT * FROM
__InstanceCreationEvent WITHIN 60 WHERE TargetInstance ISA
'Win32_Process'"), __EventConsumer subclass
(CommandLineEventConsumer with CommandLineTemplate,
ActiveScriptEventConsumer with ScriptText, NTEventLogEventConsumer), and
__FilterToConsumerBinding linking the two by references. Mechanism: WMI
service (wmiprvse.exe) polls the filter query at WITHIN interval, fires
the consumer when matched. Persistence: the filter/consumer/binding
instances survive reboots in
%SystemRoot%\System32\wbem\Repository\. Detection: Sysmon EID 19
(WmiFilter), EID 20 (WmiConsumer), EID 21 (WmiBinding); defender can
also enumerate via Get-WMIObject -Namespace root\subscription -Class
__FilterToConsumerBinding.
clusters.technical_anchor: __EventFilter + CommandLineEventConsumer + __FilterToConsumerBinding triad in root\subscription namespace; WQL WITHIN polling interval; Sysmon EID 19/20/21

clusters.canonical_name: Image File Execution Options (IFEO) Persistence
clusters.rationale: Singleton coverage-gap: SEC670 covers IFEO persistence with dedicated Lab 4.3 IFEOPersist; T-017 lacks IFEO entry.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 covers IFEO persistence with a dedicated lab (Lab 4.3: IFEOPersist)
and lists IFEO alongside services, port monitors, and WMI event
subscriptions as a peer persistence mechanism. The vault's T-017 suite
does not include IFEO. The card should document:
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution
Options\{target.exe}\Debugger (REG_SZ path to attacker binary) — when
CreateProcess(target.exe) is called, the kernel reads the IFEO key and
substitutes the Debugger value as the actual process launched, with
target.exe as argv[1]. Variant: GlobalFlag with
FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT (0x200) triggers Silent Process Exit
monitoring and can chain via
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\SilentProcessExit\
{target.exe}\ReportingMode=LocalDump + MonitorProcess. Detection: Sysmon
EID 7 (ImageLoaded) shows Debugger binary loaded in place of target;
registry monitor on the IFEO key path catches the Debugger value write.
clusters.technical_anchor: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options\{target.exe}\Debugger (REG_SZ); GlobalFlag FLG_MONITOR_SILENT_PROCESS_EXIT (0x200) SilentProcessExit chain
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton but flagship T-017 has explicit gap; well-known persistence vector.

clusters.canonical_name: Registry Run Keys Persistence

HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run,
HKLM\...\Run, HKCU\...\RunOnce, HKLM\...\RunOnce, HKLM\...\RunOnceEx,

clusters.technical_anchor: HKCU/HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run (REG_SZ command line); HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon\Userinit (comma-separated chaining)

clusters.canonical_name: Implementation Language Diversity as Signature Opsec
clusters.rationale: Singleton cross-source convergence: SEC670 recommends building offensive toolsets across multiple languages (C, C++, Rust, C#, Go) and multiple compilers for diverse static signatures.
clusters.consolidated_description:
SEC670 explicitly recommends building offensive toolsets across multiple
languages (C, C++, Rust, C#, Go) and even multiple compilers to produce
diverse static signatures, calling out Rust as increasingly critical for
evading C/C++-focused AV/EDR signatures. The card should document the
static signature surface for each language: C/C++ binaries leak CRT
symbols (memset, _security_init_cookie), compiler-specific stubs
(__main, ___main), and runtime library string literals; C# binaries emit
metadata tokens and System.Reflection usage (high entropy
distinguishable from native code); Go binaries carry runtime strings
(runtime.main, goroutine scheduling, reflect.Value); Rust binaries emit
panic_str, core::panicking, and unique cargo build-graph signatures.
Diverse languages reduce the AV signature overlap: an EDR with a strong
Rust heuristic may miss a Go implant while a C# heuristic may miss a
Rust implant. Implementation: build a single technique (e.g., process
hollowing) in C++ + Rust + Nim + C# as separate tooling paths and
rotate.
clusters.technical_anchor: Per-language static signature surface: C/C++ CRT symbols (memset, _security_init_cookie), Rust panic_str/core::panicking, Go runtime.main/goroutine strings, C# System.Reflection metadata tokens
clusters.priority_reason: Singleton opsec-principle card; lower operational specificity.
